title_en: Another ETF Triple Crown? Plus a Global Bull Market and More
title_zh: ETF 又要三冠王？全球牛市、并购潮与旗舰指数争夺战
subtitle_zh: 本期 Trillions 探讨 ETF 有望连续第二年包揽交易量、资产与新发行三项纪录，并盘点全球牛市、Goldman 并购、旗舰指数之争与希腊市场的暖心回归。
summary_zh: 本期 Trillions 由主持人搭档 Bloomberg Intelligence 分析师 Athanasios Sarafegas（代 Eric Balchunas 出镜），围绕 ETF 谈五大主题。一是三冠王（交易量、资产、新发行三项年度纪录）：今年有望连续第二年全部刷新，资金流入超一万亿美元，连续十四个月单月新增不低于一千亿美元，预计九月前后破纪录。二是牛市全球化：各国股市普涨，美国仅居中，Colombia、Greece、Peru 等非 AI 市场因价值与分散化需求亮眼，亚洲更偏科技。三是并购：Goldman 以略高于 20 亿美元收购管理约 300 亿美元、专注期权收益的 NEOS，意在追赶 JPMorgan，看重其黏性资产与分销渠道。四是旗舰指数之争：State Street 的 SPYM 借 Trump accounts 成为默认选择、费率降至两个基点；BlackRock 与 State Street 以更低价对标 QQQ，挑战 Invesco 的垄断。五是希腊复苏：经历 2015 年以来艰难重组后近年跻身前列，Global X 的 GREK 是主要追踪 ETF。
description: Another ETF Triple Crown? Plus a Global Bull Market and More

speakers.2: Athanasios Sarafegas（嘉宾，Bloomberg Intelligence ETF 分析师，代 Eric Balchunas）

turns.en: Bloomberg Audio Studios, podcasts, radio news. And when we talk about the Triple Crown, are we just barely eking past it last year's triple crown? Or or is there the potential that this is going to be a pretty watershed triple crown?
turns.zh: Bloomberg Audio Studios，播客、广播、新闻。当我们谈论三冠王（Triple Crown）时，我们只是勉强超过去年的三冠王吗？还是说，这一次有可能成为一个相当具有里程碑意义的三冠王？

turns.en: Oh? I think he's would be a watershed yere. Now again, granted what happens with the market, but flows were already over a trillion, which I think we just throw around that number trillion dollars kind of rare. Yeah, welcome to Trillions. I'm Joel Webber and I'm Athanasio, Sarah Vegas.
turns.zh: 哦？我觉得这会是一个具有里程碑意义的年份。当然，这也取决于市场接下来的走势，但资金流入已经超过一万亿美元了——我觉得我们随口就抛出一万亿美元这个数字，其实它相当罕见。好的，欢迎收听 Trillions。我是本集主持人，这位是 Athanasios Sarafegas。

turns.en: We're in mid August right now, which means A. We're also already well into Q three and B vacation schedules. Eric Bulchiunas is off this week, so we've turned to one of our favorite regulars on Trillions, Athanasio Sera Fegas, an ETF analyst with Bloomberg Intelligence who will.
turns.zh: 现在是八月中旬，这意味着：第一，我们已经深入第三季度了；第二，也到了休假季。Eric Balchunas 这周休假，所以我们请来了 Trillions 最喜欢的常客之一——Bloomberg Intelligence 的 ETF 分析师 Athanasios Sarafegas，他将……

turns.en: Be covering for Eric.
turns.zh: ……代替 Eric 来做这期节目。

turns.en: Athan. Pleasure to be doing this episode of Trillions with you.
turns.zh: Athan，很高兴能和你一起做这期 Trillions。

turns.en: Yeah, man, this, I'm excited the film for Eric.
turns.zh: 是啊，老兄，我很兴奋能来替 Eric 顶班。

turns.en: And since Eric is away, we figured we could get a little experimental. There are five storylines that we're gonna explore together.
turns.zh: 既然 Eric 不在，我们想着可以做点实验性的尝试。有五条主线，我们要一起探讨。

turns.en: Today.
turns.zh: 今天。

turns.en: Some we've briefly touched on before, others are totally new and noteworthy.
turns.zh: 有些我们之前简单提过，有些则是全新的、值得关注的。

turns.en: It might be summer, but it's not quiet and ETFs there's always something going on.
turns.zh: 虽然是夏天，但 ETF 领域可一点都不安静，总有事情在发生。

turns.en: Of course, money is flowing into ETFs at a pace we've never seen before. Back to back triple crowns. Maybe the bull market has gone totally global. Some unexpected markets and countries are capturing investors' attention. M and A is also turning heads, and Goldman Sacks is now a big reason why. There's also a competition for Marquee real estate and finally a heartwarming comebackstory, this time on Trillian's Five Big Themes and ETFs. Right now, all right, Dathan, The first thing I want to talk to you about is something that Eric and I kind of neglected to do, which was a halftime report, which usually we would do back in June. The main thing I wanted to call out was the triple crown. Triple crown is three things, and last year set records, and that was for trading volume, assets and launches. Those three things make up the triple crown. We've had triple crowns before, but the one thing we never had is a triple Crown in back to back years. How likely is that looking.
turns.zh: 当然，资金正以前所未有的速度流入 ETF。背靠背的三冠王。也许牛市已经彻底全球化了。一些出人意料的市场和国家正在吸引投资者的关注。并购（M&A）也在引发热议，而 Goldman Sachs 现在正是其中的一大原因。还有对旗舰指数这块黄金地段的争夺，最后是一个暖心的东山再起故事——这就是本期 Trillions 关于 ETF 的五大主题。好，Athan，我想和你聊的第一件事，是 Eric 和我之前有点疏忽没做的——也就是年中报告，通常我们会在六月做。我最想点出的是三冠王。三冠王指三件事，去年它们都创下了纪录，分别是交易量、资产规模和新发行数量。这三项构成了三冠王。以前我们也有过三冠王，但唯一从未有过的，是连续两年都拿下三冠王。现在看来这有多大可能？

turns.en: It's looking very likely. I think it's going to set all the records, probably by September. But you know, last year was pretty amazing. The market was good, everyone had their foot on the gas for launches, so we really thought coming into this year we weren't going to be able to repeat. It was almost like a euphouric year. But this is blowing away our expectations. And usually volume spikes when the market is bad, right, and we have a good market this year, you have launches following up, you have new issuers still coming into the market. So I think in the next month or so we could likely just already set all the records.
turns.zh: 看起来非常有可能。我觉得所有纪录都会被打破，大概到九月就能实现。你要知道，去年已经相当惊艳了：市场很好，所有人都踩足油门发行新产品，所以我们原本以为今年没法重现，去年几乎像个亢奋到极点的年份。但今年的表现完全超出了我们的预期。通常交易量是在市场糟糕时才会飙升，对吧？而今年市场很好，新发行紧随其后，还有新发行人不断入场。所以我觉得未来一个月左右，我们很可能就已经把所有纪录都刷新了。

turns.en: We've talked about Corgy and a new asset management firm that's just blown everything out of the water, could set a record and even have the most ETFs under management by the end of the year. If we removed Corgi from the picture, what does the Triple Crown start to look like?
turns.zh: 我们聊过 Corgy，这家新的资产管理公司简直把其他所有人都甩在了身后，可能创下纪录，甚至到年底持有数量最多的 ETF。如果把 Corgy 从图景中拿掉，三冠王会是什么样子？

turns.en: Launches wise, it's still really good, but they're definitely a big part of it. But you know, most of the stuff that's coming out, it's still continue to be single stock. It's derivative, it's a lot of that stuff, so that definitely skews the launches. But Corgy's definitely a big driver of it. So some of the record months that we had this year was because of Corgy. But yeah, they're definitely an interesting one. They're going with this like basically, let's put like every chip down that we can and see if one ETF hits.
turns.zh: 从新发行来看，即便没有他们，情况依然很好，但他们绝对是其中很大的一部分。你要知道，现在问世的大多数产品仍然是单只股票类的，是衍生品那一类，所以这确实拉高了发行数据。而 Corgy 绝对是一大推手。今年一些创下纪录的月份，就是因为 Corgy。不过，他们确实很有意思。他们的打法基本上就是：把手里能押的筹码全押上，看看哪只 ETF 能爆红。

turns.en: And when we talk about the triple crown, are we just barely eking past it last year's triple crown or or is there the potential that this is going to be a pretty watershed triple crown?
turns.zh: 当我们谈论三冠王时，我们只是勉强超过去年的三冠王，还是说这次有可能成为一个相当具有里程碑意义的三冠王？

turns.en: Oh? I think this would be a watershed year. Now again, granted what happens with the market, but flows were already over a trillion, which I think we throw around that number a trillion dollars. Its kind of rare. Yeah, it's And another thing we looked at is how many months taken over a hundred billion and at like new assets. It's not basically every month, this is the new norm. Fourteen straight months, we've taken at least one hundred billion every single month, which is an insane number.
turns.zh: 哦，我觉得这会是一个具有里程碑意义的年份。当然，这还要看市场接下来怎么走，但资金流入已经超过一万亿了——我觉得我们随口就抛出一万亿美元这个数字，其实它相当罕见。是的。我们还看了另一个指标：有多少个月的新增资产超过了一千亿美元。基本上每个月都是，这已经成了新常态。连续十四个月，我们每个月都至少流入一千亿美元，这是个疯狂数字。

turns.en: What was it like before those fourteen months?
turns.zh: 在这十四个月之前是什么情况？

turns.en: Very rarely it's maybe like seventy eighty, but it started creeping up so rarely did you see one hundred billion dollar month That was like in a really really good one. Now it's just the norm. Fourteen in a row. Yeah, and so this just seems like this is this is the new number of money coming in.
turns.zh: 很少见，也许就是七百、八百亿的水平，但后来开始慢慢往上爬。以前你很少能看到单月一千亿美元，那得是非常非常好的月份才行。现在这就是常态，连续十四个月。是的，所以看起来这就是资金流入的新基准数字了。

turns.en: And if there's any piece of the triple crown that doesn't set a record, what do you think it's going to be.
turns.zh: 如果三冠王里有任何一项没能创下纪录，你觉得会是哪一项？

turns.en: It might have to be volume, But really they're all Cohen. You know, unless launches stop today and there's no more launches, then that one won't happen. But that's unlikely to happen. Now. Maybe closures could potentially pick up, just because obviously with more products it's more competitive, it's harder to get these hits. But right now, I don't think any of them are gonna They're all going to be blown away.
turns.zh: 可能要数交易量了。但说实话，三项都在同步发力。你知道，除非今天发行全部叫停、不再有新产品，否则发行那一项不会出问题，但这不太可能发生。现在，清盘（closures）倒有可能增加，因为显然产品越多竞争越激烈，打造爆款就越难。但就目前而言，我觉得没有哪一项会掉队——三项纪录都会被大幅刷新。

turns.en: Okay, well one to watch. Okay, topic number two, we're going to talk about the bull market goes global. I thought this was really interesting because we've talked before and Eric is very dubious that there's anything contrary to us exceptionalism, But it turns out that the rest of the world looks pretty darn good.
turns.zh: 好，值得关注的点。第二个主题，我们来聊聊牛市走向全球。我觉得这个特别有意思，因为我们之前谈过，Eric 对美国例外论（US exceptionalism）存在任何反例这件事是非常怀疑的，但结果发现，世界其他地方看起来也相当不错。

turns.en: So far this year, it's just been like good stock markets for literally everybody. And yeah, we looked at it and the US just kind of ranks in the middle. And this is a fourteen percent gain, still a good a good year by any standards. But if you look at the average country, ETF is about up about twelve percent this year and a lot of Mungo country. Yeah, so single one. But even if you look at the broader benchmarks, they're all doing really well. So and you look at some of these smaller countries, they don't have any AI, right, not like US. What's an example of one, so like one like Colombia. Actually Greece, not to be biased, but Greece is having a fantastic year. Doesn't have any Athans Greek for the record, Yeah, if anyone could figure that out, they're a great market. So Peru. All these countries are doing really really well and have almost.
turns.zh: 今年到目前为止，几乎是所有人的股市都表现很好。是的，我们看了一下，美国大概排在中间位置。这是 14% 的涨幅，按任何标准都仍是不错的一年。但如果你看平均的国家 ETF，今年大约上涨 12%，很多单一国家也是这样。即便看更宽泛的基准指数，它们也都表现非常好。再看一些小国家，它们根本没有 AI，对吧，不像美国。举个例子吧，比如 Colombia（哥伦比亚）。其实还有 Greece（希腊）——不是我偏心——希腊今年表现出色。希腊根本没有 AI，顺便说一句，Athan 本人就是希腊人。是啊，如果有人能搞清楚这点，那它真是个很棒的市场。还有 Peru（秘鲁）。所有这些国家都表现非常好，而且几乎没有……

turns.en: No table those are those aren't AI. So what's driving it for them?
turns.zh: 没错，这些都不是 AI 驱动的。那是什么在推动它们？

turns.en: I think it's one value, Like the value factors doing really well in these countries just tend to be really kind of loaded towards that factor. But I think it's also a little bit of a diversifying trade. Yeah, we're still very skewed towards the US. I think people are starting to open up a little bit towards international just as a diverse fire against AI. You know, in case, you know, you have that month in July where AI was, you know, semiconductions were hit kind of hard. I think they're looking for a little bit of safety, and I think this is why some of these other countries are doing doing it pretty well.
turns.zh: 我觉得一是价值（value）。价值因子表现非常好，而这些国家的市场往往就重仓偏向这一因子。但我觉得这也有一点分散化交易的意味。是的，我们仍然非常偏向美国，但我觉得人们开始稍微向国际资产敞开一点，作为对 AI 的一种分散对冲。你知道，以防万一——比如七月那个月，AI、半导体被打击得挺惨。我觉得他们是在寻找一点安全感，这也是为什么其他一些国家表现不错的原因。

turns.en: Does that account for some of the inflows? Is a US money that is looking for international exposure totally?
turns.zh: 这能解释一部分资金流入吗？是美国的资金在寻找国际敞口吗？

turns.en: If we break down ETF flows, it's definitely still very very US focused. But global and international are having record years too, but so is the US. But it's just more money being spread around. And I think that also locally these countries that investors are getting much more easier access to their own stocks, So I think that's also helping fuel these country ETF performance.
turns.zh: 如果我们拆解 ETF 的资金流，它肯定仍然非常非常集中于美国。但全球和国际类也在创下年度纪录，美国同样如此，只是有更多的钱被分散到各处。而且我觉得，在当地，这些国家的投资者也更容易买到本国的股票了，所以我认为这也在助推这些国家 ETF 的表现。

turns.en: The ones you rattled off there are Columbia, Greece, slip Peru. These aren't Asian countries. And I'm curious, like, what's the Asia segment looked like in the single country stuff.
turns.zh: 你刚才报出的那些是 Colombia、Greece，还有 Peru。这些都不是亚洲国家。我很好奇，在单一国家这块，亚洲的部分表现如何？

turns.en: Asia looks really good. Obviously Korea was a big one just but that was pretty semiconductor driven, and China's been doing well. Again that's tech, so you do have tech also doing well. So Asia is definitely more skewed towards the tech side versus Europe or Latam that will have less of that. But again it just goes back to everything is doing well. Almost every sector is doing really well too. Most sectors are beating the SMP. Most stocks in the S and P are doing better than the index. So when you actually break it down, it actually is a pretty healthy market. A lot of things are just doing really really well.
turns.zh: 亚洲看起来非常好。显然 Korea（韩国）是个大亮点，但那主要是半导体驱动的；China（中国）也一直表现不错，那同样是科技。所以科技这块也表现很好。因此，相比欧洲或拉美（Latam），亚洲明显更偏向科技一侧，后者的科技含量会少一些。但归根结底还是那句话：什么都在涨。几乎每个板块都表现非常好，多数板块都跑赢了 S&P，S&P 里多数股票都跑赢了指数本身。所以真正拆开来看，这其实是一个相当健康的市场，很多东西都在实实在在地大涨。

turns.en: But of course when things go up and keep going up for a long time, makes people in see hence why there's money looking for potential international offerings.
turns.zh: 但当然，当东西一直涨、涨了很久，就会让人不安，这也是为什么有资金在寻找潜在的国际产品。

turns.en: Yeah, I think, you know, to diversify or go into things like buffer ETFs and stuff like that, just or extain money market funds. I think, you know, just as a way to you know, maybe feels a little fragile for a lot of people, and they want to make sure they don't give back a lot of these gains that they've had over the last couple of years.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得，要么去分散投资，要么买入像缓冲型 ETF（buffer ETFs）之类的东西，或者干脆放到货币市场基金里。我觉得对很多人来说，市场可能感觉有点脆弱，他们想确保不会把过去几年积累的涨幅大量回吐。

turns.en: Okay, topic number three, m and A. We haven't had a lot of M and A in the ETF space, historically, but there's been some recent.
turns.zh: 好，第三个主题，并购（M&A）。历史上 ETF 领域的并购并不多，但最近出现了一些……

turns.en: Activity that I felt was noteworthy.
turns.zh: ……我觉得值得关注的活动。

turns.en: What's been happening.
turns.zh: 最近都在发生些什么？

turns.en: So this happened last week. Goldman had bought this etfshure in NEOs, which they kind of specialize in eos. Yeah, and eos which is actually a Greek word. Oh yeah, there it goes. It's agree And I actually just watched the Odyssey this week it too, It's a very Greek filled week. I knew this was going to happen that we've been talking about. Agree, that's right. So Goldman had just bought this firm of NEOs and so they specialized in option income. METFS paid a little over two billion for them, have about thirty billion in assets. And what's interesting about this is Goldman had just acquired Innovator about like six months ago. They'd done two acquisitions in a really short time. But what stuck out to us about this was just the size of NEOs, right, being a thirty billion dollar asset manager when you kind of look at, okay, potential targets, I probably wouldn't have had Nios on the list honestly, just too big, right, and you have to pay a lot for them, So we'd maybe be thinking somewhere ten billion fifteen billion makes it more attractive. But I think now if these other issuers are looking potentially for an acquisition, I think now it puts a lot more firms in play, right, And I get it. Golden was pretty aggressive with this, Like you're not seeing this kind of aggress like aggressive movement from all some of the other firms.
turns.zh: 这事发生在上周。Goldman 买下了 ETF 发行人 NEOS，他们专门做期权收益类产品。NEOS 其实是个希腊词。哦对，又来了——它是希腊语，意思是新。我这周还正好看了《奥德赛》（Odyssey），真是个充满希腊味的一周。我就知道我们会聊到希腊。好，言归正传：Goldman 刚买下 NEOS 这家公司，他们专攻期权收益型 ETF，Goldman 为此付了略高于 20 亿美元，NEOS 管理着约 300 亿美元的资产。有意思的是，Goldman 大约六个月前才刚收购了 Innovator，短短时间内做了两笔收购。但真正让我们注意的是 NEOS 的体量——一家 300 亿美元的资产管理公司。当你去列潜在收购标的时，说实话我大概不会把 NEOS 放进名单，因为它太大了，你得为它付很多钱。我们可能更倾向于 100 亿到 150 亿这个区间，那样更有吸引力。但我觉得，现在如果其他发行人也在考虑收购，这就把更多的公司拉进了可被收购的行列。我理解，Goldman 这次相当激进——你不会看到其他所有公司都有这么激进的动作。

turns.en: What's what's happening at Goldman? Why would they want to do this?
turns.zh: Goldman 到底在打什么算盘？他们为什么想做这件事？

turns.en: Goldman was interesting when they kind of launched around the same time with JP Morgan, and they were kind of going head to head as these two big banks and their assets are pretty neck and neck. But then after a while, just you kind of felt Goldman give up, you know it just and JP Morgan really took off. JP Morgan really leaned into it.
turns.zh: Goldman 很有意思：他们差不多和 JPMorgan 同时入场，作为两大银行正面交锋，资产规模一度不相上下。但过了一阵子，你会感觉 Goldman 有点放弃了，而 JPMorgan 则真正起飞了，JPMorgan 全力投入了进去。

turns.en: Of the big banks, JP Morgan has the most assets under management.
turns.zh: 在大银行里，JPMorgan 的资产管理规模最大。

turns.en: Yeah, and most of them are in like Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley, So you do have most of the Wall street banks in the industry. But JP Morgan just really ran away from everyone. So Goldman in a way might be trying to catch up, like hey, we you know, maybe before they just thought that ETFs weren't worth it, you know, Obviously the fees are low and we're a much bigger bank.
